subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: AES — The Global Standard
description: Learn AES — The Global Standard in one minute.

hook.text: The US government held a global competition to choose the world's next encryption standard. Belgium won.

buildup.text: In 2001, the Advanced Encryption Standard replaced the aging DES cipher for protecting classified data.

discovery.text: AES uses symmetric keys of 128, 192, or 256 bits. AES-256 has more possible keys than atoms in the universe.

twist.text: AES is so strong that even the NSA uses it for top-secret documents. No practical attack has ever broken it.

climax.text: One algorithm protects your Wi-Fi, your bank, your phone, and classified government secrets equally.

punchline.text: More keys than atoms. Still unbroken today.

quiz.question: Why is AES-256 considered extremely secure?
options: It has more possible keys than atoms in the observable universe
It changes the key every microsecond
It requires quantum computers to encrypt
